question: What is the atomic number of nitrogen?
solution:
The correct answer is __**7.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• ATOMIC NUMBER: 

 
 
• ​It is defined as the number of protons present in the nucleus.
 
• It is denoted by the letter Z.
 
 
 
• MASS NUMBER: 
 
 
• ​The total number of protons and neutrons present in a nucleus is called the mass number of the element.
 
• It is denoted by the letter A.
 
 
 
• **For neutral atom,**
 
 
• Number of protons in an atom = Z
 
• Number of electrons in an atom = Z
 
• Number of nucleons in an atom = A
 
• Number of neutrons in an atom = N = A – Z
 
 

CALCULATION__:

 
• Given – A = 14 and Number of electrons in an atom (e) = 7
 
• As we know that the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons in an atom. Therefore, the number of protons is 7.
 
• 
 
As we know that, Mass number (A) = Number of protons (p) + Number of neutrons (n)

 
∴ n = A – p

 ⇒ n = 14 – 7 = **7**
